title: Add halt-attenuator admission and proactive region-hedger probe to reduce SLO oscillation
author: Aisha Gupta
description:
Motivation: We have observed transient SLO oscillations during short-lived regional saturation events where aggressive admission and circuit resets cause noisy reopen cycles. This PR introduces a lightweight admission component (halt-attenuator) that smooths immediate hard halts by applying a short, decaying attenuation window to rate/admission decisions and a proactive region-hedger probe that detects imminent cross-region egress pressure and biases routing away from a fragile region before full failover is required. The goal is to reduce SLO oscillation, avoid circuit flapping, and preserve KV cache locality where possible so tail-latency and token-cost budgets remain stable.

What this changes (high-level):
- New runtime admission guard: HaltAttenuator (server/runtime/admission/halt_attenuator.go) which intercepts per-request admission decisions and applies a decaying attenuation factor for the first N seconds after a detected hard halt. The component does NOT replace the circuit breaker; it softens the immediate binary halt to a probabilistic attenuation for low-priority routes.
- RegionHedger probe (controlplane/hedger) that periodically samples regional egress metrics (egress_qps, local_kv_pressure, circuit_open_ratio) with a configurable window and emits a soft routing weight delta to the smart router. The hedger is conservative by default: it only nudges weights when multiple signals cross thresholds.
- Two feature flags and runtime knobs: runtime.feature.halt_attenuator (off|canary|on) and hedger.probe.window_ms and hedger.hedge_threshold. Canary defaults deploy to 5% traffic in selected regions.
- Telemetry: new metrics (halt_attenuator.attempts, halt_attenuator.allowed_ratio, hedger.weight_nudges, hedger.probe_latency_ms) and a new structured audit log when attenuation is applied so SRE can correlate attenuation events with SLO deltas.
- Tests: unit tests for attenuation decay math and integration test simulating short halts with synthetic KV pressure. Performance microbench for low-overhead path added.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- We intentionally keep attenuation probabilistic (sample/allow) rather than queueing requests to avoid head-of-line queuing in overloaded workers. That keeps latency bounds predictable for requests that are allowed through.
- The hedger is advisory only; routing decisions are ultimately decided by the router which now accepts a weight_delta from hedger. This separation keeps the hedger low-privilege and easy to toggle if we observe adverse effects.
- We do not change global circuit-breaker semantics; this is an intermediate smoothing layer meant to reduce oscillation frequency and improve graceful degradation UX.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main feature-flagged off.
2) Canary: enable runtime.feature.halt_attenuator=canary and hedger in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 at 5% for 48h with increased telemetry retention. Monitor halt_attenuator.allowed_ratio, hedger.weight_nudges and SLO 99th latency.
3) Gradually increase canary to 25% then 50% with staged regions.
4) If any region shows increased error_rate or SLO regressions, revert flag for that region and escalate.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for attenuation decay and hedger decision logic
- [x] Integration test simulating KV pressure and short halts
- [x] Bench microtest to validate <0.5% p99 overhead on hot path
- [x] Telemetry dashboards and alert runbook additions under observability-pack/dashboards/halt_attenuator.yaml
- [x] Linear tasks linked (ENG-4307)

Why this is different from previous soft-fallback attempts: Prior work focused on coarse-grained tenant quarantines or immediate failover. This PR targets the "in-between" window: the few seconds after a hard halt decision where a short smoothing action avoids triggering coordinated failovers or noisy reopen cycles. The hedger extends that by proactively steering away from regions showing early signs of instability rather than waiting for a full circuit open event.

review_comments: Marcus Lee: Nice approach. Two immediate concerns: 1) Do we have any scenario where attenuation could worsen tail by letting through expensive slow requests? 2) Can hedger produce oscillation if multiple hedgers in sibling regions nudge weights against each other?

Author (Aisha Gupta): For (1) we limit attenuation to low-priority routes by default; metric halt_attenuator.allowed_ratio will be exposed per-route so SRE can inspect. For (2) hedger uses a conservative vote model (requires two signals) and adds a randomized backoff on nudges to avoid synchronized flips. Added a comment in region_hedger.go explaining the anti-oscillation backoff.
Evan Michaels: Add a fast opt-out flag scoped to deployment/unit-tests so we can flip the hedger quickly during canary. Also add more integration scenarios with mixed-priority traffic.
Author (Aisha Gupta): Added runtime.feature.hedger_opt_out and extended integration test to include mixed-priority driver. See tests/integration/short_halt_sim_test.go commit c3d4e5f.
Priya Nair: Telemetry looks good; request we add a composite SLO dashboard panel showing allowed_ratio vs 99p latency to simplify post-canny analysis.
Author (Aisha Gupta): Added panel to observability/dashboards/halt_attenuator.yaml and a short runbook step in docs/reliability/hedger.md.
